description: Hand-written: the traversal.* stateful rows’ own contract (PL.native-traversal-rows slice 2, U106(1); core’s P9e layers, P9e.core) — the personal-vehicle and lent-mode rows over core’s functions (the state one row answers is what the next is sent), the save block’s writer and reader, and one traversal.session: core’s TraversalPlanner, VehicleRegistry and FastTravelDirector wired together with a StaminaPool, scripted geometry and locomotion hosts, a recording clock and bus, every op it takes, the host op restating the scripted answers, a save loaded back, core’s degradations with no hosts, and the rows’ own refusals as errors coded [invalid-input]. Every expectation here was computed by core’s own functions and classes at the pin, not by these rows. Core’s own corpora (conformance/traversal/{session,mounts,save}.json, 62 cases) are driven whole through these rows by the traversal_corpus ctest (tests/traversal_corpus.cpp), not transcribed here.

cases.name: traversal.personal: each row is one of core’s personal-vehicle functions, the pack’s params read on every call; the state a verb answers is what the next verb is sent
traversal.personal: the rows’ own refusals are errors coded [invalid-input]
traversal.lending: each row is one of core’s lent-mode functions; an actor’s own mode is never taken back
traversal.save: the block a save stores (core’s writer, at core’s extension key) and core’s reader, whose refusals are values
traversal.session: core’s planner, registry and director wired as one session; each op one core call with what the hosts recorded, a save loaded back
traversal.session: no probe, no locomotion host, no meter, no seed — core’s own degradations; the view is the four layers’ state
traversal.session: the rows’ own refusals are errors coded [invalid-input]; an unknown op names the known ones

steps.expectError: the session was created with no probe
the session was created with no locomotion host
